season_storylines: Patrick Mahomes is back at practice rehabbing the torn ACL/LCL from Week 15 last season while KC pivots run-heavy after making Kenneth Walker III the highest-paid RB free agent ever at 3yr/$43.3M, making Walker a non-PPR goal-line gold mine and Mahomes a discount-only QB.

A.J. Brown was traded from Philadelphia to New England for a first-round pick, joining Romeo Doubs, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Kevin Byard in an all-in Patriots build with a 10.5 win total, and his downfield TD profile travels perfectly to non-PPR.

Tyreek Hill was released by Miami and remains unsigned amid reports of no power in his surgically repaired left leg after the dislocated knee and torn ligaments, so he should be off draft boards entirely until a signing and clean medicals.

Mike McDaniel is now the Chargers offensive coordinator under Harbaugh, installing wide-zone runs, heavy motion and the quick game, which lifts Justin Herbert, makes Omarion Hampton the lead back in a friendlier scheme, and turns Ladd McConkey into a yardage engine.

Kyler Murray, traded to Minnesota, took 16 of 22 first-team snaps over the weekend and is trending to beat out J.J. McCarthy, and a rushing QB throwing to Justin Jefferson is exactly the ceiling profile a 6-pt-passing-TD league pays for.

The QB carousel reshuffled half the league: Tua Tagovailoa (Falcons, holding off rehabbing Michael Penix Jr.), Geno Smith (Jets, on a short leash ahead of rookie Cade Klubnik), Kirk Cousins (Raiders, bridging No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza) and Deshaun Watson vs Shedeur Sanders in Cleveland where Watson has thrown multiple practice INTs already.

San Francisco lost Ricky Pearsall to a season-ending injury days after signing Mike Evans, consolidating targets on Evans whose 17-yard-per-catch, red-zone-dominant profile is tailor-made for non-PPR even at his age.

Detroit has a double flag: Jahmyr Gibbs is seeking a new deal while nursing a back issue Dan Campbell calls non-serious, and Sam LaPorta is 10 months out from lower-back microdiscectomy, whose absence last year fueled the Jameson Williams and Gibbs target spikes (verify Gibbs camp participation before drafting at cost).

Jaylen Waddle was traded to Denver where Sean Payton projects him well past the 376 routes he ran in Miami, with beat projections near 122 targets and 1000-plus yards, a clean yardage-based buy in this format.

Betting markets set Baltimore and the Rams as co-favorites at 11.5 wins, with the Rams adding Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie to build a top DST, while Arizona sits at a league-low 3.5 wins, capping the environment around top rookie RB Jeremiyah Love.

teams.outlook: Jacoby Brissett bridges to rookie Carson Beck on a 3.5-win team, so the fantasy play is volume not environment: No. 1 rookie RB Jeremiyah Love should out-snap James Conner and Tyler Allgeier while Trey McBride and Marvin Harrison Jr. soak targets.

Kevin Stefanski's ground-heavy scheme (verify) plus an unsettled Tua-vs-rehabbing-Penix QB room means Bijan Robinson is the offense, a monster non-PPR bell-cow with goal-line work, while the pass catchers are capped.

New 29-year-old OC Declan Doyle brings Payton/Ben Johnson motion and shot plays that Lamar Jackson has publicly praised, keeping Lamar the format's premium rushing QB, but Mark Andrews' career-low 1.23 YPRR makes him a name-brand fade.

Josh Allen remains elite in 6-pt-TD scoring on rushing TD equity alone, but Joe Brady's bottom-quartile pass volume and a WR-by-committee featuring a declining DJ Moore (YPRR 2.31 to 1.24 over three years) caps every Bills receiver.

The backfield is the story: Chuba Hubbard managed just 3.8 YPC post-injury and Jonathon Brooks returns from his second ACL after a 2025 redshirt, so whoever wins goal-line work is the only Carolina back worth non-PPR draft capital.

DJ Moore's exit condenses targets on Luther Burden III (2.69 YPRR as a rookie on a limited route share), Rome Odunze and TE Colston Loveland (23 percent target share from Week 8 on), though Caleb Williams' 58 percent completion rate keeps the floor shaky.

Cincinnati rebuilt its 32nd-ranked defense with Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen and is favored in 15 of 17 games, which may trim shootout volume slightly but keeps Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Chase Brown in the league's best TD environment.

Neither Deshaun Watson (multiple practice INTs) nor Shedeur Sanders has seized the job, and two early-round rookie WRs (KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston) threaten Harold Fannin Jr.'s 21 percent target share, so treat every Brown as a late-round dart.
Javonte Williams parlayed an RB11 season into a top-40 ADP, and while non-PPR hides his league-worst 0.40 YPRR as a receiver, he is TD-dependent at a price that assumes repeat goal-line luck.

Sean Payton traded for Jaylen Waddle and projects him toward 122 targets after Miami buried him at 376 routes, making Waddle the clearest yardage-based WR buy, with Troy Franklin vs Pat Bryant deciding the WR3 scraps.

Jahmyr Gibbs' contract standoff and back tweak plus Sam LaPorta's return from back surgery cloud the pecking order, while trade addition Isiah Pacheco replaces David Montgomery as the complementary hammer, so confirm Gibbs' camp status before paying his first-round price.

Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks left, condensing routes on Christian Watson, who has averaged 17.5 FPG when running 75 percent-plus of routes, a classic non-PPR deep-threat profile, with first-rounder Matthew Golden and slot-bound Jayden Reed behind him.

Houston imported David Montgomery specifically to fix a league-worst 17 percent TD rate inside the 5, so he is a pure goal-line TD bet entering his Year 8 age curve, while Wyatt Teller and Braden Smith upgrade the line for C.J. Stroud.

Alec Pierce's ankle rehab limits the field-stretching role early, Josh Downs' slot volume matters less at zero PPR, and TE Tyler Warren's play-action usage is the sneaky TD path; the Seth McGowan vs DJ Giddens battle sorts the backfield depth (verify lead-back hierarchy).

Travis Hunter is fully cleared from his torn LCL for a full two-way workload, and with Travis Etienne gone the backfield tilts to 4.32-speed Bhayshul Tuten over Chris Rodriguez Jr. (foot procedure), giving Tuten big-play non-PPR appeal.

Mahomes is practicing but rehabbing ACL/LCL surgery and the offense reoriented around record signing Kenneth Walker III, whose implied goal-line monopoly in an Andy Reid offense is elite non-PPR currency, while 37-year-old Travis Kelce and a McDuffie-less defense both slide.

OC Mike McDaniel's wide-zone, motion-heavy install is the league's best scheme upgrade: Herbert gains easy completions, Omarion Hampton profiles as the every-down zone runner, Ladd McConkey feasts on YAC, and David Njoku arrives as the red-zone TE.

The Rams sit atop the market at 11.5 wins after landing Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie, making their DST a top-tier big-play unit in this scoring, with the veteran offensive core intact around Puka Nacua (verify QB workload plan through camp).

Kirk Cousins starts while No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza develops, and record-paid center Tyler Linderbaum stabilizes the interior, but a 5.5-win total says this is a volume-starved offense where only the lead back and top target are draftable (verify backfield pecking order).

A full teardown: Tua, Waddle and Tyreek are gone, Malik Willis starts on a make-or-break deal, and a 4.5-win total plus big-play regression risk makes De'Von Achane a fade at cost since zero-PPR strips his catch-volume floor.

Kyler Murray took 16 of 22 first-team snaps and is trending toward the job over J.J. McCarthy, and his rushing floor plus Justin Jefferson gravity makes him a 6-pt-TD league value, with Jauan Jennings added as a physical complement.

New England traded a first for A.J. Brown and added Doubs, Vera-Tucker and Byard to a 10.5-win roster, so Brown's contested-catch TD profile is a top non-PPR WR bet and the passing offense rises across the board, with the RB3 job behind Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson open.

Travis Etienne signed as the lead back and rookie Jordyn Tyson adds juice outside, but an unsettled QB room and 7.5-win projection make Etienne's volume the only reliable non-PPR asset (verify Week 1 starting QB).

New OC Matt Nagy's Reid-tree structure plus Malik Nabers back at practice from injury gives Nabers top-five WR upside, with Jaxson Dart's rushing ability, Cam Skattebo's between-tackles role and Isaiah Likely's red-zone arrival all TD-friendly.

Geno Smith starts with an explicit win-or-sit mandate ahead of rookie Cade Klubnik, so Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall carry week-to-week QB variance, while the Minkah Fitzpatrick and Demario Davis additions prop up a sneaky DST.

New OC Sean Mannion's Shanahan-style system expands Saquon Barkley's role and goal-line monopoly, but that same shift shrank Jalen Hurts' rushing line to 105-421-8 last year, cutting directly into the Konami ceiling this format pays for; DeVonta Smith inherits the A.J. Brown target vacuum.

Mike McCarthy takes over the offense (verify) with trade addition Michael Pittman and signee Rico Dowdle, but the QB plan is genuinely unsettled, so Pittman is a volume bet and Dowdle a TD-dependent flier until a starter is named (verify QB).

Zach Charbonnet and Kenny McIntosh open camp on PUP, leaving George Holani as the likely Week 1 starter with rookie Jadarian Price pushing, a cheap path to early-season non-PPR RB volume on a 10.5-win roster.

Mike Evans' arrival and Ricky Pearsall's season-ending injury consolidate the passing tree, but Christian McCaffrey enters his age-30 season off 400-plus touches, a profile that has produced one top-5 repeat in 13 years, so pay for Evans' TDs and not CMC's history.

New OC Zac Robinson's McVay-tree offense elevates Emeka Egbuka into the clear lead role (WR9 in PPG early last year), but Baker Mayfield's contract standoff, Chris Godwin's health and the Vita Vea trade request add real turbulence (verify Mayfield camp status).

Brian Daboll's RPO and play-action vertical scheme is a direct upgrade for Cam Ward after his record-setting rookie passing yardage, with Calvin Ridley, Wan'Dale Robinson and rookie Carnell Tate forming a deeper target tree while JC Latham rehabs on PUP.

Washington spent on defense (Rasul Douglas, Leo Chenal, Odafe Oweh) and added TE Chig Okonkwo, but a modest 7.5-win market number says the offense projects closer to average, keeping Jayden Daniels' rushing TDs the roster's one premium format asset (verify offensive line health).

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: Consensus best player in the rookie class walks into Arizona's lead role over aging Conner and Allgeier; rookie-contract volume plus goal-line touches is the exact non-PPR profile that wins leagues even on a bad team.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Was WR9 in points per game early last season and now gets a clear lead role in Zac Robinson's McVay-tree offense; yardage-and-TD scorers love McVay-style layered routes.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: Posted 2.69 YPRR as a rookie, third-best since 2011, on under 70 percent route share; DJ Moore's departure hands him full routes, and his YAC style produces yardage this format pays for.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's wide-zone scheme replaces Greg Roman's plodding run game in LA; Hampton projects as the every-down back in a rising offense with goal-line equity.

breakout_watch.name: Ladd McConkey
breakout_watch.why: McDaniel's offense is engineered to manufacture YAC, and McConkey's separation skill converts that into raw yardage, which matters far more here than his catch totals.

breakout_watch.name: Jaylen Waddle
breakout_watch.why: Traded to Denver where Payton projects him near 122 targets after Miami capped him at 376 routes; his downfield efficiency with a real offense is a pure yardage buy.

breakout_watch.name: Christian Watson
breakout_watch.why: Averaged 17.5 fantasy points per game across 13 games with a 75 percent-plus route share, and the Doubs/Wicks exodus finally hands him those routes; a deep threat with TD equity beats any slot compiler in this format.

breakout_watch.name: Colston Loveland
breakout_watch.why: Commanded a 23 percent target share from Week 8 on in an offense that runs the second-most 13 personnel; late-season role plus red-zone size equals a TE breakout.

breakout_watch.name: Kyler Murray
breakout_watch.why: Trending toward the Vikings job with 16 of 22 first-team snaps; rushing yardage at 10 yards per point plus 6-pt TDs to Justin Jefferson is a top-8 ceiling at a mid-round price.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Ward
breakout_watch.why: Set the first-year passing yardage record despite a bad staff, and Brian Daboll's play-action vertical scheme plus Ridley, Wan'Dale and rookie Carnell Tate is a real supporting cast upgrade.

breakout_watch.name: Kenneth Walker III
breakout_watch.why: Kansas City made him the richest RB free agent signing ever while pivoting run-heavy during Mahomes' knee rehab; an Andy Reid goal-line monopoly is elite non-PPR currency.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Etienne's exit and Chris Rodriguez's foot procedure clear the Jacksonville lead role for the 4.32-speed back; his big-play rushing profile needs zero receptions to pay off here.

breakout_watch.name: Travis Hunter
breakout_watch.why: Fully cleared from the torn LCL for unrestricted two-way work; his downfield target profile plus potential return-adjacent usage fits every quirk of this scoring.

breakout_watch.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
breakout_watch.why: Led Cleveland with a 21 percent target share as a rookie; even with two rookie WRs drafted, a chaotic QB room historically funnels targets to the safety-valve TE, and his price is free.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Age-30 season directly after 400-plus touches; only one back in 13 years has followed that workload with a top-5 finish, and his receiving cushion is worth less at zero PPR.

fade_watch.name: Patrick Mahomes
fade_watch.why: Rehabbing torn ACL and LCL, back at practice but with a run-shifted offense built around Kenneth Walker III; projected as a third-tier QB, so pay backup-level price or pass.

fade_watch.name: Travis Kelce
fade_watch.why: Turns 37 in-season with his QB coming off major knee surgery and the offense reallocating resources to the ground game; name-brand ADP, declining TD equity.

fade_watch.name: Jalen Hurts
fade_watch.why: Rushing line already shrank to 105-421-8 as Philly hands Barkley the goal line, and a new OC leans further into the RB screen game; the rushing ceiling that justified his price is evaporating.

fade_watch.name: De'Von Achane
fade_watch.why: Big-play efficiency regression plus a gutted Miami offense led by Malik Willis, and non-PPR erases the reception floor that props up his ADP.

fade_watch.name: DJ Moore
fade_watch.why: Three straight years of YPRR decline (2.31 to 1.24) lands him in Buffalo's bottom-quartile-volume, committee-based pass game; possession profile with fading yardage is the worst archetype here.

fade_watch.name: Javonte Williams
fade_watch.why: RB11 finish inflated his ADP to the 3-4 turn, but he was dead last in receiving YPRR among busy backs and his season leaned on TD conversion that historically regresses.

fade_watch.name: Mark Andrews
fade_watch.why: Career lows in YPRR (1.23) and YAC per reception, a new play-caller, and Baltimore's bottom-5 pace; the TD spikes that made him elite are the first thing age takes.

fade_watch.name: David Montgomery
fade_watch.why: Explicit goal-line role in Houston keeps him non-PPR relevant, but Year 8 age curve and three straight years of declining carry share make him strictly a TD bet, not an every-week starter.

fade_watch.name: Tyreek Hill
fade_watch.why: Released by Miami, unsigned, with reports of no power in the surgically repaired left leg after the dislocated knee; do not draft on name recognition (verify any signing and medicals).

uncertainty_note: Genuinely unsettled as of August 3: the Minnesota (Murray vs McCarthy), Cleveland (Watson vs Sanders) and Atlanta (Tua vs rehabbing Penix) QB rooms; Mahomes' practice workload and Week 1 readiness off ACL/LCL surgery; contract standoffs for Baker Mayfield and Jahmyr Gibbs (plus Gibbs' back); recovery timelines for Malik Nabers, Sam LaPorta, Chris Godwin and Michael Penix Jr.; Pittsburgh's starting QB; and the Seattle backfield until Charbonnet and McIntosh clear PUP -- preseason games will move all of these.
